inspection_summary: Inspected all 691 normalized lines. The usable mathematical text runs through the definition and motivation of zeta moments, Heath-Brown's fractional-moment theorem and convexity construction, two heuristics and the random-matrix model for moment constants, and conditional and unconditional progress toward sharp bounds. Extracted formulas have occasional layout damage, but every accepted mechanism is recoverable from checked prose and adjacent expressions; the malformed absolute-value/power expression near line 174 is explicitly flagged for scan verification. Front matter, acknowledgements, references, page furniture, and a brief list of undeveloped external applications were accounted for but not promoted to units.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the survey's scope and high-level conditional/unconditional moment-bound landscape; no standalone semantic unit beyond material developed later.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Heath-Brown's work on fractional moments of zeta(s)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines moments, relates them to pointwise bounds and RH, records the sharp-order target, and develops Heath-Brown's convexity-based fractional-moment mechanism and its transfers.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Conjectures for moments of zeta(s)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops Dirichlet-coefficient and Gaussian heuristics, states the Keating-Snaith constant, explains the random-matrix representation, and separates arithmetic from universal symmetry factors.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Progress: conditional upper bounds
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Organizes the three progress directions and explains Soundararajan's two-range and Harper's multiscale prime-polynomial methods under RH.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2-3.3. Unconditional upper and lower bounds and applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States upper- and lower-bound propagation principles from twisted moments and notes an alternative large-deviation route and broader applications.

accepted_units.title: Moments as an average-to-pointwise bridge
accepted_units.why_material: Defines shifted and critical-line moments and explains that the full family of near-linear moment bounds is equivalent to Lindelof, while RH supplies a stronger zero-location premise with prime-distribution consequences. This fixes why moment growth is an informative proxy for extreme values rather than merely an integral statistic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions of zeta and I_k and the surrounding motivation; the prime-counting example continues immediately after this span in the next unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the definitions and implications are clear in prose, but the extracted displayed sums and integrals must be retained with their notation.

accepted_units.title: Conditional, convexity, and subconvex pointwise regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Places RH-implied subexponential control, unconditional convexity, and successive subconvexity exponents in one hierarchy. The comparison exposes how analytic continuation and functional symmetry give a baseline and how improvement below that baseline becomes a distinct structural problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the strong PNT error-term consequence referenced at the end of the preceding unit and then focuses on pointwise zeta bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: several exponents and the prime-counting display are formula-sensitive; prose makes the implication hierarchy recoverable despite PDF line wrapping.

accepted_units.title: From known moments to the sharp-order moment problem
accepted_units.why_material: Shows the historical shift from using moments to control extremes, through exact low moments and a high-moment bound, to the general target T(log T)^(k^2). It distinguishes inaccessible full asymptotics from the weaker but structurally sharp upper and lower order-of-magnitude goals.
accepted_units.context_note: Carries the narrative through the pre-Heath-Brown ranges and stops just before the theorem statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: exact moment indices, powers, and inequality directions depend on the displays, which are legible though vertically fragmented.

accepted_units.title: Fractional moments despite the nonregularity of zeta powers
accepted_units.why_material: States Heath-Brown's rational/unconditional and real/conditional ranges and identifies the central obstruction: fractional powers of zeta need not be regular, so ordinary Cauchy contour deformation is unavailable. Gabriel convexity is introduced as the replacement move.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the parameter cases u/v that organize the ensuing construction; the actual surrogate and smoothed comparison are in the next unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the range distinctions are formula-dependent but clearly supported by prose and the theorem list.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet surrogate, discrepancy, and smoothed convexity comparison
accepted_units.why_material: Approximates zeta^k through a finite divisor Dirichlet polynomial S, packages the mismatch as g=zeta^u-S^v, and compares smoothed functionals J, K, and L. Mean-value control of L plus Gabriel convexity transfers estimates between the critical line and a shifted line, turning the nonregular fractional-power problem into tractable surrogate and error terms.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is kept intact because the definitions, comparison inequalities, mean-value scale, convexity transfer, and removal of the smoothing tails jointly form one mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact powers and absolute-value delimiters are essential, and the extraction near line 174 is malformed. The prose and adjacent inequalities recover the conceptual mechanism, but the original scan should be checked before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Convexity machinery transfers beyond the original global moments
accepted_units.why_material: Documents that the reusable contribution was not only a larger theorem range but a convexity method subsequently adapted to short intervals, uniformity in the moment parameter, derivative inequalities, Dirichlet L-functions, value distribution, and other L-function families.
accepted_units.context_note: The short-interval results provide a concrete transfer instance; the terminal citation list is evidence of breadth rather than separate mechanisms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the short-interval lower bounds require the extracted displays, while the transfer claim is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Truncated Dirichlet coefficients predict the moment exponent and arithmetic factor
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from a convergent shifted-moment mean value, moves it toward the critical line by truncating at the analytic conductor scale, and obtains the k-squared logarithmic exponent together with an Euler-product factor a_k. It isolates prime arithmetic as one component of the conjectural constant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first of two independent order-of-growth heuristics and includes the definition of a_k needed later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the generalized divisor coefficients, truncation, gamma normalization, and Euler product are carried by displays whose reading order is imperfect but recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Selberg Gaussian fluctuations independently predict k-squared growth
accepted_units.why_material: Treats log|zeta| as approximately Gaussian and applies its exponential moment, converting variance proportional to log log T into the same T(log T)^(k^2) scale. This supplies a probabilistic representation of the exponent independent of the coefficient truncation.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument is explicitly heuristic because it assumes a sufficiently uniform Selberg central limit theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the variance and Gaussian moment-generating identity determine the exponent; the extracted formulas are legible but split across lines.

accepted_units.title: Keating-Snaith completes the moment constant
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the conjectural leading constant into the arithmetic factor a_k and a second factor g_k, then states the Barnes-G formula valid for positive real k and its factorial specialization for integer k. This upgrades isolated guessed constants into a uniform law.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical failure of earlier heuristics beyond small integer moments so the generality of the conjecture is visible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the normalization by Gamma, Barnes-G quotient, and integer product formula must be read exactly from the displays.

accepted_units.title: Zero statistics select a unitary characteristic-polynomial model
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers Montgomery's local zero-statistics analogy to unitary eigenphases, matches mean densities to choose matrix size N approximately log(T/2pi), and replaces zeta by det(I-U). Evaluating characteristic-polynomial moments then produces the g_k factor and the k-squared polynomial degree.
accepted_units.context_note: The chain from scaled zeros to group integral is retained as one unit because omitting density matching would make the representation choice look arbitrary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: zero/eigenphase scalings, density matching, determinant, and group integral are formula-dependent; surrounding prose keeps the chain interpretable.

accepted_units.title: Reconciling universal matrix statistics with prime arithmetic
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies a limitation of the pure matrix model—a_k has to be inserted—and records hybrid Euler-Hadamard and full moment-polynomial approaches that recombine primes and zeros or predict lower-order structure beyond the leading coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact polynomial claim here is stated for integer k and remains conjectural.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the leading-coefficient normalization and polynomial degree are display-dependent, while the prime/zero limitation is explicit prose.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry type transfers the moment model across L-function families
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how zero distributions in families select unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal compact groups, allowing the characteristic-polynomial recipe to generalize by symmetry type. It also records distinct multiple-Dirichlet-series and long-Dirichlet-approximation routes to the same family of conjectures.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a concise survey-level transfer map rather than a derivation of any family-specific constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: compact-group names and the central-point location matter, but the conceptual transfer is prose-complete.

accepted_units.title: Three routes toward sharp moment bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Organizes progress into conditional high-moment upper bounds, unconditional small-moment upper bounds, and unconditional all-moment lower bounds, then locates Soundararajan's almost-sharp and Radziwill's sharp-range conditional results within that map.
accepted_units.context_note: The taxonomy is retained because the next mechanisms solve different sides and ranges of the same conjectural scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the exact logarithmic loss and range endpoint are formula-sensitive and slightly cramped in extraction, but the result directions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Prime-sum majorants and asymmetric control of small and large primes
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH, upper-bounds log|zeta| by a prime-supported Dirichlet polynomial plus a truncation penalty, splits primes into two scales, and trades computable high moments of small-prime sums against variance control for large primes. Markov bounds on large values convert these controls into an almost-sharp zeta moment estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Equation (11) supplies the majorant; the prose immediately after it explains the two-scale allocation of moment budget.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the weighted von Mangoldt sum and log T/log x penalty are central; PDF extraction fragments the denominator but the checked prose fixes its role.

accepted_units.title: Harper's multiscale Taylor and exceptional-set iteration
accepted_units.why_material: Refines the two-range method into many prime blocks, assigns decreasing powers as prime size grows, approximates exponentials by truncated Taylor polynomials on good sets, and shows bad blocks occur on sets too small to matter. Flexible truncation and length choices keep each resulting Dirichlet polynomial inside available mean-value theorems.
accepted_units.context_note: The detailed beta_j, P_j, exceptional sets, and truncated-series inequality are included because together they explain why the iterative budget closes rather than merely naming a decomposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several thresholds, exponents, and the truncated Taylor expression are extraction-sensitive. The prose preserves the architecture, but exact constants should be checked against the scan before formal reuse.

accepted_units.title: Twisted anchor moments propagate unconditional upper bounds downward
accepted_units.why_material: Formulates the principle that computing a moment with room to spare—equivalently with a short Dirichlet-polynomial twist—can yield sharp upper bounds for smaller moments. The zeta implementation combines an iterative scheme with a twisted fourth-moment input to reach the full interval from zero to two.
accepted_units.context_note: The earlier discrete fractional ranges are included to show what the propagation principle improves.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the operative principle is prose-complete; exact k-ranges and the fourth-moment anchor are notation-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Twisted mean values propagate lower bounds on both sides of the first moment
accepted_units.why_material: Summarizes how short Dirichlet-polynomial twists turn a computable mean value into sharp lower bounds above an anchor and how a twisted second moment also reaches below the first moment. It contrasts this interpolation-like route with an independent route through lower bounds for large deviations in Selberg's central limit theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical coverage of k at least one and then zero below k at most one so the final all-positive-moment closure is explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the direction of propagation and anchor moments are clear in prose, while exact ranges depend on the displayed k notation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic and universal factors in moment constants
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The coefficient truncation isolates the prime-dependent factor a_k, while unitary characteristic-polynomial moments isolate g_k; hybrid prime-zero models explain why both factors are required in the same conjectural constant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a synthesis of heuristics and conjectures, not a proof of zeta moment asymptotics, and the full polynomial statement cited is restricted to integer k.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Surrogates plus rare-failure control across upper-bound methods
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both the earlier convexity argument and later prime-polynomial methods replace a difficult fractional zeta expression by tractable Dirichlet data, then control the discrepancy either analytically or by proving the exceptional set is negligible.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The discrepancy function in Heath-Brown's method and the exceptional blocks in the later RH-conditional methods are technically different objects; the shared pattern does not transfer their hypotheses or estimates automatically.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Twisted anchor moments as bidirectional range extenders
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A moment computable with a short Dirichlet-polynomial insertion acts as an anchor: upper bounds propagate to smaller moments, while suitable first- and second-moment anchors propagate lower bounds above and below the first moment.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The survey states these principles only roughly; exact admissible twists, errors, and family hypotheses must be recovered from the cited works before theorem-level use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Average-to-extreme duality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source uses moments to constrain pointwise extremes in one direction and pointwise majorants plus tail estimates to bound moments in the other, making distributional control and extreme-value control mutually informative.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equivalence with Lindelof needs the full family of integer moment bounds, while the prime-sum majorant route is conditional on RH and does not supply a symmetric equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry-guided representation selection
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Local zero statistics and density matching select a compact-group characteristic-polynomial model, and the symmetry type of an L-function family determines which group supplies its universal moment factor.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The representation is conjectural and does not by itself recover the prime-dependent arithmetic factor or prove transfer for any specific family.
